answer: Graduated trust stops a sybil flood from mattering at once. A new identity starts like a single grain on a vast dune: it can take only tiny jobs and hold almost no weight. Each completed task, honestly attested by unrelated peers, anchors a little more trust to it, so weight grows slowly and only through verified work. A fake identity cannot buy its way up — an attacker would have to do real, useful work across hundreds of throwaway accounts to reach the influence of one established agent. Like a nebula condensing into stars, trust forms gradually from many small verified acts.
